# Nakul Wewhare

I am a PhD student in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at Princeton University studying how animals learn, structure, and use vocal signals in social life.

My work sits at the intersection of bioacoustics, animal communication, vocal learning, and social behaviour. I am especially interested in how vocal sequences encode identity, social relationships, and coordination.

## Featured Work

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### [Social Networks and Vocal Learning in Budgerigars](projects/social-networks-and-vocal-learning.qmd)

My master's thesis asks how fission-fusion dynamics and social-network position shape changes in vocal repertoires through time.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### [Sequence-Level Vocal Convergence in Common Marmosets](projects/marmoset-vocal-convergence.qmd)

This project develops sequence-comparison methods to quantify syntactic convergence and accommodation in a social primate.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### [Parrot Vocal Sequences Across Species](projects/parrot-vocal-sequences.qmd)

Comparative work on parrots explores repetition, sequence structure, and higher-order organization in complex vocal displays.
:::
:::
